day: Friday of week 23 in Ordinary Time
text:
There is a curious tension in today's readings, and it sits very close to the truth of how we live as followers of Christ. Paul speaks with urgency and intensity about discipline, about running the race with purpose, about making his body obey him. He has given everything over to the gospel, holding nothing back. Yet in the Gospel, Jesus cautions us about the very thing that such dedication can produce: the blindness that comes from self-righteousness, the plank in our own eye that we refuse to see while we fixate on the splinter in someone else's.

Paul's honesty helps us here. He does not claim to have arrived. He speaks of discipline not as proof of his perfection but as the ongoing work of staying true to what he has been called to do. He knows himself well enough to fear being disqualified. This kind of clear-eyed self-knowledge is what Jesus is calling for too when he speaks of the plank we cannot see. The work is not to judge our brother; it is to look at ourselves first, truthfully, without flinching.

Perhaps the invitation today is simply to notice where we are running hard but losing sight of ourselves, where we are so certain of our vision that we have stopped looking inward. What might shift if we paused to ask: what am I not seeing about myself?
